name: Leafy Green
lede: Leafy Green is a plain, descriptive plant name from the 2010 xkcd color survey, close enough in the color graph to [[kelly-green|Kelly green]] and [[kelly-green|Kermit Green]] that all three sit in the same patch of yellow-green.

sections.title: A crowd's plant word
sections.body:
The name is exactly what it describes: the green of a leaf, with no further story behind it in our sources, and our graph records its origin as a 2010 xkcd crowd-survey name [1]. In that same 2010 survey, respondents also produced [[kelly-green|Kermit Green]] and reused the older brand name [[kelly-green|Kelly green]] for colors that, in the graph, sit within 3.3 units of this one [1]. [[grass|Grass]] is close as well, at 3.7 units, nearly the same green by a different everyday word, with [[leaf|Nasty Green]] a little further out at 4.0 [1].

Computed by ISCC-NBS block, Leafy Green falls as a vivid yellowish green, matching the family [[kelly-green]] and [[kelly-green]] also land in [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive holds this color covering at least 1 percent of its canvas, within a color distance of 4, as photographed [2]. That absence puts it alongside its closest relatives, Kermit Green and Kelly green, both likewise rare in museum paint: bright, saturated survey greens like these have no real pigment history, so painters never needed them [2].
